preconditions.description: n, k, and x are within the specified bounds.
Each element in the array a satisfies the absolute value constraint.
The array a has exactly n elements.

postconditions.description: The output array b has exactly n elements.

postconditions.expression: all((b_i - a_i) % x == 0 for b_i, a_i in zip(b, a))
postconditions.description: For each element, b_i ≡ a_i mod x holds true.

postconditions.expression: sum(1 for b_i, a_i in zip(b, a) if b_i != a_i) <= k
postconditions.description: The total number of operations (changes) applied to the array is at most k.

postconditions.expression: all(b_i == a_i + m_i * x for b_i, a_i in zip(b, a) for m_i in [0, 1, -1, 2, -2, ...])
postconditions.description: Each b_i is derived from a_i by adding or subtracting multiples of x (including zero).

postconditions.expression: product(b) <= product(b_prime) for all possible b_prime satisfying Q1, Q2, Q3, and Q4
postconditions.description: The product of the elements in b is the minimum possible among all valid configurations.

candidate_issues.task_evidence: he invented positive integer x and decided to add or subtract it from arbitrary array elements... the operation may be applied more than once to the same position.
